event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Uber’s 2024 Form 10-K positions COVID-19 primarily as a medium-term, still-relevant threat.  Management acknowledges both (i) concrete, historical damage – most notably the sharp collapse in global Mobility demand, driver-supply shortages, and market-wide financial-market volatility suffered in 2020-2022 – and (ii) ongoing, forward-looking uncertainty around new waves, vaccine efficacy, labour availability, consumer-behaviour shifts, supply-chain stresses and capital-market access.  The company also highlights second-order organisational consequences, such as two years of compulsory remote work and the challenges of a permanent hybrid workforce.  Language is specific (describes demand destruction, travel behaviour, financial-market impacts) and explicitly links the pandemic to material adverse effects on revenue, liquidity and human-capital management.  Because the pandemic’s onset (March 2020) is now four years distant, the Time Decay Principle tempers severity scores into the moderate band (4-6).  Nevertheless, the filing makes clear that COVID-19 remains a live risk driver across operations, finance, labour and strategic planning; hence the extracted snippets cluster toward the upper end of the medium-term range.

evidence_list.snippet: Outbreaks of contagious disease and the impact of actions to mitigate such disease or pandemic, have adversely impacted and could in the future adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly states past adverse impact (‘have adversely impacted’) linking directly to company’s business and financials.
Projects continuing future impact (‘could in the future adversely impact’) showing ongoing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Sentence acknowledges both realised and prospective harm from pandemics; specificity on business-wide effects pushes score to a solid mid-level 5.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the pandemic and responses thereto had an adverse impact on our business and operations, including, for example, by reducing the demand for our Mobility offerings globally, and affecting travel behavior and demand, as well as impacting Driver supply constraints.

components.reason: Cites concrete operational impacts (global demand reduction, travel behaviour shifts, driver-supply constraints).
Uses definitive past-tense (‘had an adverse impact’) confirming materiality.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed enumeration of specific operational harms justifies a strong but still time-decayed score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent of the impact of any future pandemic or outbreak of disease, on our business and financial results will depend largely on future developments, including the duration of the spread of the outbreak and any future “waves” or resurgences of the outbreak or variants of the virus, both globally and within the United States, the administration, adoption and efficacy of vaccines in the United States and internationally, the impact on capital and financial markets, the impact on global supply chains, foreign currencies exchange, governmental or regulatory orders that impact our business and whether the impacts may result in permanent changes to our end-users’ behaviors, all of which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted.

components.reason: Enumerates multiple forward-looking risk channels (new waves, vaccines, supply chains, capital markets, consumer behaviour).
Emphasises high uncertainty, reinforcing potential severity.
Purely conditional language without past loss data.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive list of prospective pandemic variables earns a moderate score of 4, limited by lack of concrete financial figures.

evidence_list.snippet: Our employees worked from home for almost two years in light of the pandemic, and although we have implemented our “return to office” plan, which includes a shift to a hybrid model where employees have flexibility to work from home, a hybrid model may create challenges, including challenges maintaining our corporate culture, productivity and availability of key personnel and other employees necessary to conduct our business, increasing attrition or limiting our ability to attract employees if individuals prefer to work full time at home or in the office.

components.reason: Links pandemic to prolonged remote-work regime and specific workforce risks (culture, productivity, attrition).
Expresses forward-looking challenges post-pandemic hybrid model.
No direct financial quantification; impacts framed as ‘may’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights labour-management risk rooted in pandemic experience; qualitative nature keeps score at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Outbreaks of contagious diseases or other viruses could lead to a sustained decline in the desirability of living, working and congregating in metropolitan areas in which we operate.

components.reason: Connects pandemic outbreaks to long-term demand deterioration in key urban markets.
Use of ‘could’ signals uncertainty rather than certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Urban-demand risk is material but stated hypothetically; after time-decay the snippet scores at the low-moderate edge.

evidence_list.snippet: Concerns over the economic impact of the pandemic caused extreme volatility in financial markets, which adversely impacted our stock price and our ability to access capital markets, and any future pandemics or other catastrophic events may have a similar impact.

components.reason: Identifies concrete past financial-market effects (stock price drop, capital-market access).
Projects recurrence in future pandemics, expanding risk horizon.
No numeric magnitude and phrased partly hypothetically.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct link between pandemic and capital-market volatility merits a 4, moderated for lack of figures and medium-term timing.
